newsitem.title: CHINA: Canada, China sign C$4.0 bln nuclear power deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada, China sign C$4.0 bln nuclear power deal.

text.p: Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd and China National Nuclear Corporation on Tuesday signed a contract for construction of two 700-megawatt CANDU-6 nuclear reactors worth C$4.0 billion, Canadian officials said.
China's Premier Li Peng and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien witnessed the signing ceremony at a hotel in a suburb of Shanghai, they said.
The two reactors will be built at Qinshan, Zhejiang province about 80 km from Shanghai.
The agreement is the largest single commercial deal between China and Canada.

Of the sale, the Canadian content amounts to C$1.5 billion and will generate an estimated 27,000 direct and indirect person-years of employment in Canada over the six-year construction period, the Canadian consulate said in a statement.

"It is Canada's hope that this contract will mark the beginning of a long-term commercial relationship between Canada and China in the peaceful and safe use of nuclear energy," Chretien said in remarks released by the consulate.
The Export Development Corporation would provide financing for the Canadian component of the sale, the statement said.
The total project would involve partners from Japan, the United States and Republic of Korea and would be co-financed by the national export credit agencies of the other partner countries, it said.
A Canadian official said the Export Development Corporation of Canada would provide the funding on a commercial basis at the OECD consensus basis rate of 7.49 percent over 15 years.
A Canadian diplomat said Tuesday's signing was the last link in a chain that began in November 1994 with a bilateral agreement between Chretien and Li Peng in Beijing in November 1994.
"Over the last six months there have been very tight negotiations on terms and conditions," he said.
